loading.note: eager in the header when light is the site's default scheme, or when no dark image is set, since the light image is then shown in both schemes; otherwise lazy, as it always is in the footer (SC-019, SC-025). The header is above the fold on every page, so lazy loading would delay the logo the page shows and the largest contentful paint with it. Eager, not fetchpriority=high: that is the one priority image's (section#priority-media), and loading="eager" is what both platforms can write, where next/image cannot omit the attribute without claiming priority (SC-019).

eager in the header only when dark is the site's default scheme; otherwise lazy, as it always is in the footer (SC-019, SC-025). An eager image is fetched whether or not it is shown, so the scheme the page does not arrive in never has an eager logo. Eager, not fetchpriority=high: that is the one priority image's (section#priority-media), and loading="eager" is what both platforms can write, where next/image cannot omit the attribute without claiming priority (SC-019).

elements.when: a light and a dark image are set

notes.text: The link is named once by aria-label and both images are alt=""; WordPress's light image alt and dark image aria-hidden go.

Of the header's two logos, only the default scheme's is eager; the other scheme's is lazy, so a page does not fetch an image it does not show (SC-025). The default scheme is the one the document arrives in before any script runs: dark where the site offers dark mode and sets it as its default, otherwise light, which is also what a site that follows the visitor's system gets, since the server cannot know the visitor's scheme. A visitor script then puts in the other scheme loads that logo lazily, in view. With no dark image the light one is shown in both schemes and is the eager one.

owes: data-swaps instead of has-dark; name on the link; --logo-height inline.
SC-019, SC-025: in the header, the default scheme's logo carries loading="eager" and the other scheme's loading="lazy"; the footer's are both loading="lazy".
SC-019, SC-025: in the header, the default scheme's logo carries loading="eager" and the other scheme's stays lazy; next/image lazy-loads both by default.
